summary: Root plays like a fable about power: each faction has a completely different rulebook and win condition, so the Marquise's engine-building race feels nothing like the Vagabond's solo questing or the Eyrie's rigid, self-punishing card program. Games are tense and swingy, with the leader getting dogpiled and board states shifting fast once someone starts scoring points.
praised: asymmetric factions that each feel like a different game
tight 60-90 minute playtime for its depth
criticised: steep teaching burden since every player needs to learn a different faction
brutal to newer players who don't understand threat assessment
runaway leader problem if the table doesn't gang up
Eyrie's forced moves can feel punishing

interaction.detail: Players fight over the same shared map of clearings, and battles, crafting, and card denial constantly push and pull at each other's plans. Nearly all meaningful state (the map, item supply, card market) is shared and contested rather than sitting on private boards.

scoring.why: Each faction races up a shared victory-point track using its own distinct VP-generating engine, and the game can also end via a faction-specific dominance or coalition condition instead of pure points.
scoring.how_you_win: Reach 30 victory points before anyone else, earned through faction-specific actions like building, battling, crafting, or completing quests, or trigger your faction's special dominance/coalition victory.
